Great to meet this morning. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Integration surface we discussed
   - Primary use: structured output + tool-calling for ticket routing and automated responses.
   - Secondary: embeddings + reranker for semantic search over KB.

2) Technical follow-ups you asked for
   - SDK setup & auth: we support API keys (short-lived recommended) and OIDC for enterprise.
   - Routing: per-route model pinning and regional fallback.
   - Structured output/tool calling: JSON schema enforcement + function calling patterns.
   - Embeddings & rerankers: batching recommendations and cosine distance thresholds.

3) Rate limits / retries / idempotency (high priority for your infra team)
   - We recommend adding an idempotency key (X-Request-ID or Idempotency-Key) for any stateful write.
   - For 429s: exponential backoff with jitter and retry-after respect.
   - Quotas: per-API-key quotas and per-route per-minute caps 21 we can provision higher bursts for Dedicated trials.

Attachments: integration_diagram.png 2
T— high-level flow we walked through.

Next steps:
   - We will send a short integration guide + retry pattern doc (Ben/Dev to add technical notes).
   - Marissa/Ben: propose a short sandbox test for embeddings + reranker this week.
   - Sarah: confirm whether you want OIDC or API-key onboarding for the pilot.

If that looks right I can set up a 30-min follow-up demo for Thurs or Fri.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Sarah 2
T— quick answers from the infra side, plus attached SLA excerpt (redwood-sla.pdf) showing burst behavior for Dedicated: 

1) Sample quotas (hosted)
   - Default per-key: 60 rps per-route, 3,600 per-minute heavy-route cap. Bursts allowed up to 300 rps for short windows (10s) depending on rate-limiting token bucket.
   - Dedicated: configurable pools; we can provision sustained 600+ rps for embeddings with reserved GPUs.

2) 429 handling: client-side retries are primary. Server returns Retry-After when we can admit more load 2
T— clients should respect that. We also support automatic routing to a lower-cost fallthrough model (less costly but compatible) when capacity constrained.

3) Idempotency: use Idempotency-Key for write endpoints (ticket creation). Keep dedupe window ~24 hours for safety, shorter (12
2 hours) often okay depending on backend. We recommend storing idempotency keys in your request metadata and using X-Request-ID for tracing.

I'll attach the SLA excerpt. We can also generate a small table with quota numbers matched to your projected TPS.

- Ben
